recipes.title: Carnivore Pizza (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Here's the best carnivore pizza in Western Pennsylvania.

Well, it would have been carnivore if I could find my regular Boursin cheese (garlic and herb) but I had to settle for Garlic and spicy honey.

Also overcooked it by a few minutes because I rolled this one really thin.

To make the crust, combine 1.5 cups shredded mozzarella with 2 tbs Boursin or cream cheese. Microwave in 30 second bursts and stir with a spatula until nice and gooey.

Quickly stir in one egg and mix well, then add 3/4 cup butter powder and 1 tbs plain or beef gelatin. Dust your dough ball with more butter powder if it's still wet.

Lay dough out and flatten with a plate on parchment atop a sheet tray. I think I made mine a little too thin.

Bake at 375 for 8 minutes and check it. If it's nice and golden flip and cook another two minutes. My mistake was cooking at 400 for 10 minutes.

My "sauce" is 1 tbs with 5 tbs sour cream, mixed with an immersion blender. I laid it on just a little too thick but it was till very tasty. Just a little goes a long way.

Top with your fav toppings and return to the oven for another 5 minutes. I transferred the pizza to a wooden platter because I didn't want the bottom getting any darker.

recipes.title: Crab-Stuffed Bacon Onion Rings
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Even the screw ups are delicious! 

I stuffed two onion rings with a new crab mix recipe I came up with and then wrapped the onion in bacon and fried it in tallow.

Unfortunately, it was a bit hard to work with because I didn’t freeze before wrapping. But it turned out really tasty!

I may try this again, but I’ll probably try them on the smoker or in the air fryer.

But before that, I’m probably going to stuff some jalapeños with this crab mix and wrap them in bacon! 

Stay tuned!

If you’re wondering about the crab mix recipe:

It’s one 1lb can of lump crab
2 tablespoons yellow mustard
Half cup pork Panko crumbs
1 tablespoon Old Bay
2 tablespoons grated Parmesan 
And the “Mayo” is One ounce soft cream cheese blended with 5 tablespoons sour cream. This mayo is really tasty!

Salt to taste

recipes.title: Beef Stew
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Another mouth watering idea that ends up costing you less than $10 per meal.

Stew meat is on sale for $7.99 a pound so I grabbed 2 pounds, browned it a little it a skillet with some oil, salt and garlic powder.

Then into the instant pot with a whole onion and a cup of bone broth for 45 minutes on high pressure and a 15 to 20 minute natural release.

It turned out fork tender and delicious. 

I repurposed all the leftover broth and poached some eggs in it. The eggs and broth were my breakfast with a little bit of the stew meat. The leftovers will be my dinner at work.

I probably won’t cook it with a whole onion next time because the onion turned out really mushy. I’ll just use onion powder next time for the flavor.

recipes.title: Cheese Sauce (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Here's how to make an easy and delicious cheese sauce for your pork rinds.

Gently warm 1/2 cup cream on low with 2 tbs cream cheese. Once that's fully dissolved, add 1 cup of shredded cheddar, a little a time.

Very important to not boil the sauce when adding the cheese. You can remove the pan from the heat for a minute if necessary. 

Boiling does something to the cheddar and it will taste fine but have a grainy texture when it cools.

Take your time and do this on the lowest heat possible because it's so worth it!

Note: You can add a little more cream if it's too thick or more cheese if it's too thin.

recipes.title: Chicken Thighs Dinner
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Here’s another easy dinner for less than $10 and that’s using high-quality chicken thighs from @BellandEvans. 

An air fryer makes quick work of making crispy skin chicken thighs but if you don’t have one, you can use the oven.

Pat your chicken dry and apply salt and herbs to the bottom of the chicken and just salt to the top. The reason is you don’t want the herbs to burn and placing herbs on top of the chicken skin is likely to accomplish that. You just want the flavor.

Place in a un oiled casserole dish and bake a preheated oven at 425° for about 40 minutes.

Turn the oven up to broil and bake the tops for another 10 minutes or so, to get the skin crispy. 

I had planned to save half of these for lunch, but they were so good that I ate them all!

recipes.title: Pizzagna (14)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I made the best Pizzagna ever but it ended up more like a lasagna bowl.

What made it the best ever was a combination of using Delallo pomodoro sauce, fresh garlic, real parm cheese, quality Italian herbs and an irresponsible amount of pizza cheese. 

Start by browning 1.5 pounds ground beef and .5 pounds ground sausage. 

Add 1 small diced onion, a tbs of Italian herbs and salt to taste.

While that's going heat up 2 cups of pomodoro sauce (or any of your favorite tomato sauce) along with 1/2 tbs of Italian herbs

I went Vesuvius with the sauce by baking the sauce after I topped it with 2 cups shredded pizza cheese and handful of freshly grated parmesan cheese.

Lay out the ground beef and top with 1-2 cups of ricotta cheese mixed with a dash of salt, a pinch of Italian herbs and a handful of shredded pizza cheese. Sprinkle that with more freshly grated parmesan.

Then comes the sauce.

I wasn't happy with the distribution of the sauce and cheese so next time I'll just lay it all out evenly in a casserole dish so every bit gets equal amounts of ricotta, sauce and cheese.

But wow, this tasted so good!

recipes.title: Carnivore Ravioli/Taquitos
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Here’s the carnivore ravioli/taquito recipe.

Melt one cup shredded mozzarella in 20 second increments until melty.

Add a half cup of butter powder and work it into the cheese. Add a tbs of raw egg. Then add up to another half cup of butter powder. Whatever it takes to get the doughy consistency you see in the video.

Flatten and bake on parchment in a 375° oven for 8 to 12 minutes. 

Add whatever filling you like and fold them over and bake for an additional five minutes but lower the temperature to 200° so you don’t darken the raviolis too much.

I used a half a pound of ground beef with one cup of ricotta cheese, seasoned with a little bit of garlic powder, onion powder and salt.

I’m thinking rolling these out with a rolling pin and lowering the cooking time might get a proper ravioli but these were pretty delicious as is.

It could also possibly be used as a flatbread sandwich or pizza.

recipes.title: Cajun Salad
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I only ate a salad today.

A Cajun salad that turned out lovely!

It's 1 cup diced Andouille sausage, 1 cup diced cooked shrimp and 2 tbs diced red onion.

The "mayo/dressing" is 2 tbs sour cream blended with 1 boiled egg and 1 tsp of cajun seasoning (Slap Ya Mama). That's half of what you will see in the video. I made way too much and a little goes a long way.

If I still ate corn, some of that would have gone in it as well. 

Eat with pork rinds or right off a spoon.

recipes.title: Bulgogi (3)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Lots of things going on in this post.

I made the best Bulgogi ever with 1/4 cup coconut aminos, half a cup of bone broth, 2 tbs kimchi paste (gochujang) and garlic powder. 

I marinated 12 oz of shaved ribeye overnight and bought a pint of steamed rice from a local Chinese restaurant.

The rice was converted into resistance starch after an overnight stay in the fridge.

Now rice usually bloats me so I only eat it a few times a year. Eating this 2 cup portion led to an half pound weight loss and zero bloat.

But what did it do to my blood glucose? The end of the video shows my reading after an hour and 50 minutes. 

This meal was my only meal of the day.

recipes.title: Probiotic Cheesecake
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Not sure you’ll find this anywhere else in the world.

It’s probiotic cheesecake ice cream and the cream in it is a cream cultured kefir. 

I’m not even sure how to name it because it has more names than a Spanish princess. 

I began by adding a tablespoon of kefir grains to one cup of heavy cream. I let that ferment for 36 hours and then strained the grains out.

Next, I warmed up a quarter cup of heavy cream in the microwave to 165° plus. I tempered 1/3 of the cream into two egg yolks, then added 2 tablespoons of cream cheese, half a tablespoon of vanilla extract, and a teaspoon of Stevia and mixed well with a hand blender.

Then I combined the egg yolk mixture with the cream kefir, transferred to Pyrex container and tried to freeze it.

I say tried because it was only in the freezer for two hours because I had a date with the river and some smallmouth bass.

The completely frozen parts reminded me of ice milk, but delicious and slightly tangy as fermented foods should taste.

But the partially frozen creamy part hit like delicious melty ice cream and won me over. 🥰

The best news is ⬇️

recipes.title: Pork Done Right
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Besides bacon, pork sucks… 

especially if you don’t know how to cook it. 

There’s nothing worse than a lean and dry pork chop but if you have a thermometer and cook it to the right temperature, I promise they can make your mouth water.

I dry brined these pastured pork chops overnight and gave them an eight minute sear with a weight, in a little tallow, for eight minutes and cooked the other side for about four minutes with no weight.

I pulled them out of the pan at 140° and resting them brought the carryover temperature up to about 145°. 

I saved all the delicious juices and cooked garlic baby Bella mushrooms with a little additional butter, while the pork chops were resting.

Who needs sides when you have an excellent topping?

recipes.title: Swordfish
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Swordfish is like chicken and pork had a baby… except somehow the baby tastes way better than either one.

It has that thick, meaty bite that almost doesn’t register as fish. Cooked to about 130–135°F, it stays incredibly juicy and tender inside.

It’s basically the steak of the sea.

Cook over hot charcoal for 6 to 7 minutes on one side and 3 to 4 on the other. You can do this in a frying pan as well with a little bit of butter.

You don’t need any special seasonings, but I do like a little bit of Old Bay on mine. 

It’s a good time of year to buy swordfish. I scored this piece for $13.99 a pound.

recipes.title: Seafood Cataplana
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
.@ChefGruel and @SecKennedy both said we should eat more seafood…  

So I refined my Cataplana recipe. I enjoyed it so much the other day that I changed a few things and doubled the size.

It’s an absolute vitamin and mineral bomb and it’s so delicious and satiating. You can even make egg drop soup with it to stretch it even further.

Cook halfway:
4 oz bacon fat 
1 large rough chop onion
2 medium chopped tomatoes 
3 tbs garlic

Add and bring to low boil:
16 oz clam juice
4 bay leaves
3 tbs Old Bay
1/2 tbs salt

Add clams/mussels and bake in a covered Dutch oven at 400° for 12 minutes:
12 oz frozen clams
12 oz frozen mussels

Add scallops and bake for 12 more minutes:
1 pound scallops

Add shrimp and bake for 12 more minutes:
12 oz shrimp

Mix in 12 ounces of smoked sausage. No need to bake it if it’s already cooked.

This will get you six generous servings. 

My total cost for all of the ingredients was $65.

recipes.title: Cataplana
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
This dish has been on my bucket list for 20 years and I’m a little mad I waited this long to try Cataplana.

It’s a traditional Portuguese dish made with seafood and pork, and the broth is stunningly delicious.

You’re supposed to use linguica, which is a type of Portuguese chorizo, but I improvised with andouille sausage. 

Start by cooking your vegetables halfway in a Dutch oven with a half stick of butter on medium heat (never cook on high heat with a dutch oven atop a stove

Half a large onion
1 bell pepper
1 large tomato 
2 cloves garlic

Add a cup of clam juice, a tablespoon of Old Bay, 2 bay leaves and bring to a low boil. 

Add

12 oz sausage slices
16 small clams
1 lb white fish
1/2 pound shrimp
2-small lobster tails

Add another half tbs Old Bay, cover and bake in a preheated oven for 20-25 minutes.

There’s no right or wrong seafood to add to this dish, but I’m probably leaving the fish out of this dish next time. It got mushy.

Also going to use chopped lobster and frozen clams because the liquid wasn’t hot enough to cook all the clams thoroughly. Probably more shrimp and maybe scallops!

Also going to use chopped lobster and frozen clams because the liquid wasn’t hot enough to cook all the clams thoroughly. Probably more shrimp and maybe scallops!

recipes.title: Muffins (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Not sure why I don’t make these carnivore “muffins” more often.

There’s just something uniquely delicious about how the flavors from the egg and the bacon gel when cooking together.

You have to try it to understand. 

Cook your bacon 400° for 12 to 15 minutes. You want it half cooked.

Ring bacon in a standard muffin pan and pour a little bit of bacon grease into each cup.

Carefully crack an egg into each ring.

Bake for exactly 10 minutes. The eggs will continue to cook as they gradually cool down.

Use a spoon to carefully extricate each of the muffins.

Enjoy!

recipes.title: Korean BBQ (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Housemate wanted me to make her Korean barbecue for her birthday and she said these were better than anything she’s ever had in an Asian restaurant.

That’s great because I tried using Mama O’s kimchi paste instead of gochujang and she didn’t even notice. 

Mama O’s has half the carbs and I can source it at Whole Foods.

The marinade is half a cup beef broth, 1/4 cup coconut amino’s, 3 tablespoons kimchi paste and a light sprinkling of salt.

That’s it!

I marinated these for 16 hrs and gave them a good mix about halfway through. I recommend at least an eight hour marination.

You can buy flanken style short ribs at Costco or ask your butcher to cut them for you. I like them exactly 3/8 of an inch thick. Any thicker and they’re a bit chewy. Any thinner and there’s not much meat on them.

recipes.title: Keto Ice Cream Sandwich
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Keto Ice Cream Sandwich!

I keep seeing local ice cream sandwiches at my co-op so I decided to try and keto something up and what I got turned out very enjoyable.

Best of all, it's only 20g net carbs.

The "lids":
1 cup finely sifted almond flour
1 egg
4 tbs melted butter
1 tbs vanilla extract
Sweetener of choice (I used allulose)

Combine and bake at 350 for 15-18 minutes in 4" round baking cups.

The "meat":
Gently warm 3/4 cup heavy cream
1/2 tbs vanilla extract
1/4 cup allulose (or sweetener of choice)

Get it tepid but do not boil and combine in stages with 2 egg yolks. Pour into 2-4" round baking cups and freeze for at least 3-4 hours.

Tips: Use a butter knife to gently loosen the lids. Same for the ice cream pucks.

I like the crust, but I’m probably going to make them half as thick next time. The good news is that will drop this to about 12 g of net carbs per sandwich.

recipes.description:
Here’s another free recipe from my cookbook.

I was going to make smoked meatloaf with carnivore gravy, but I was hungry and didn’t want to wait so I made smoked meatballs! 

The tragedy here is I only had one cup of beef stock so I could only make a small amount of gravy.

And you don’t need a grill to make these meatballs. You can cook them in the air fryer or oven at 350 for 25 to 30 minutes.

Also, the closer you keep the meatballs to the hot coals, the faster they will cook

recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Big Food's best selling Salisbury steak has 65 ingredients! Mine has seven:

2 pounds ground beef
1 small onion (a little butter to cook them in)
2 cups beef stock
1 cup heavy cream
garlic powder
salt

and it tastes 100 times better!

Omit the onion and garlic powder and it's 100% carnivore.

Start your onions and gravy reduction first.

You can reduce the stock and cream at a fairly high heat as long as you watch it. As you get toward the end, you need to watch it closely and reduce the heat because it goes from almost finished to overfinished, quick. Stir constantly!

If your stock has too much fat, the gravy will not come together. There's more than enough fat in the cream to make it tasty and satiating.

I never add salt or spices to reduction gravy while it is reducing. What tastes good at the start will be greatly intensified after it's reduced. If you want to season your gravy, do it at the very end.

The gravy will take 25 to 30 minutes, the onions take about 15 minutes. The "steak" takes about 12 minutes so start the steak about the time your onions or done (15 minutes).

recipes.title: Chili (5)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Instead of bringing the chili to the hotdog, I thought why not bring the hot dog to the chili?

Ok so I used Adell andouille sausage instead of hot dogs, but the concept is the same and the result is delicious.

I turned it into a casserole but it's really not necessary.

Took about 25 minutes to put this together and it accepts mustard very nicely!

Hot Dog Chili Casserole:
1 pound ground beef
1 small onion, diced
1 package of hot dogs or sausages
2 cups tomato sauce
1 cup beef broth
2 tbs tomato paste
2 tbs chili powder
1 tbs garlic powder
1 tbs cumin
1 tsp paprika
salt to taste

recipes.title: Pizza (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I tried @Rosettesmix pizza and bagel dough and it's a good way to treat yourself without mistreating yourself.

That is, if you can tolerate almond flour and the 40-45g of carbs that make up this entire pizza, sauce and cheese included.

You start by melting shredded cheese in the microwave, then adding one egg and then the mix.

The crust took me about 25 minutes of baking to get it how I liked it while the box said to cook it 5-10 minutes. Then it took another 15 to cook the toppings.

The end product reminded me of a peanut butter cookie combined with a pita. It's a little crumbly but more than firm enough to hold sauce and cheese.

It's incredibly filling and more than adequate to scratch a pizza itch. I still have half a bag of dough left so I'll probably make some bagels with those.

recipes.title: Steak-umm Recipe
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I think this will be my last recipe in my @steak_umm series but don't quote me.

One bite will raise your eyebrows.

Yes, it's very similar to the Steak-umm lasagna I made last week but it's much simpler.

Steak-umm Manicotti

Season and bake 6 Steak-umm sheets at 350 for 12 minutes or until just done. Allow to cool

Combine 1 cup ricotta cheese with one egg, a dash of garlic powder, a handful of shredded pizza cheese and freshly grated parm cheese and a pinch of salt.

Stuff and roll the Steak-umms with the ricotta mix. Place in a small casserole dish and top with tomato sauce or marinara, more pizza cheese and parm cheese and bake at 400 for 15-20 minutes.

recipes.title: Potato Salad
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Got the idea to make potato salad with sour cream instead of mayo from @MCOnnalin and it’s really good! 

I eat potatoes a few times a year and I’ll definitely do this again.

Cook 1 lb chunked red or golden potatoes with 1 cup water in an Instant pot for 5 minutes on high pressure and a quick release.

Put potatoes on a tray or platter and chill in fridge for 12 minutes. 

They should be a little warm when you add the sauce.

1/2 cup sour cream
1.5 tbs yellow mustard 
1 tsp any vinegar 

Add 2-3 chopped boiled eggs and The sauce to the potatoes and salt to taste. Garnish with chives and bacon bits.

About 3 portions @ 26g carbs each.

Let it chill overnight and it will have even fewer carbs the next day (resistant starch.)

recipes.title: Flanken Short Ribs
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
You can eat short ribs a number of ways but getting them cut flanken style and baking them at 400° is the fastest way to enjoy them. 

Ask to have them cut 1/4-1/2” thick. Any thicker and they can be a little chewy. These were a shade under 1/2” and were perfect in about 18 minutes.

Costco’s are closer to 1/4” which is fine but more work cooking and eating.

There’s no marinade on these but flanken short ribs will gladly accept one and take on whatever flavor you prefer in as little as an hour.

recipes.description:

I even added a can of albacore tuna and you know what?

Tunadine salad

1/4 cup diced pickles
1/4 cup sour cream
garlic powder and salt to taste.

Mash up your fishes with a fork before combining all ingredients. Eat with pork rinds, celery, bacon or whatever you can imagine.

recipes.title: Cheese Sauce (1)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
This simple cheese sauce (aka Queso Blanco) is the tastiest carnivore thing you can dip your pork rinds in and it's only 3 ingredients.

1/2 cup heavy cream
1 slice white American
an equal amount of Monterey Jack

Ok so, the tiny flecks of pepper in the MJ are not carnivore so sue me.

The American I use is from Organic Valley and there are no weird ingredients. Yes you can use different cheeses but I can't guarantee a better flavor than this combo. Experiment if you like.

I will say that when I used freshly shredded MJ it had a funny texture to it. It was still good but these precut platter pieces broke down and melted the smoothest.

This sample size recipe is tiny which makes it a perfect one person appetizer. Don't want to get loaded on chips and cheese instead of your entree!

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I can't find A2 cottage cheese anywhere so I made my own and it only cost me $2.25 for a cup's worth.

It doesn't taste like store bought cottage cheese at all and that's fine by me. It's really tasty!

Bring 4 cups milk gently to 190 degrees and remove from heat. 

Add 4 tbs white vinegar (or lemon juice) and stir.

Let sit for 15 minutes then strain. Add salt to taste and a tbs or two of heavy cream if you like it wet. I liked it dry so I did not add cream.

ChatGPT hooked me up with the recipe.

recipes.title: Butter Sandwich Stack
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
There’s something magical that occurs when you sandwich ingredients.

You don’t have to be a gourmet chef to cook a mouthwatering roast. 

You can cook it fast in a pressure cooker or slow in a crock pot. All you need is a little salt or seasoning and some broth or water.

Chuck roasts are the most popular because they have the perfect ratio of fat and protein and they turn out the most delicious.

Here’s a guide to cherry picking chucks!

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese (1)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I made @eda2026's cottage cheese. It's not quite what I was expecting but it's good. It's like cottage cheese and feta made a baby.

It's tangy, super easy to make and very low in carbs.

Grok says I don't have to boil it and that I can make this on a stovetop in a ceramic bottomed pot or double boiler. The trick is to get it between 135-175° to get the curds to separate. The lower the temp, the creamier the cheese.

I baked this at 400 for about 40 minutes, strained and cooled it for about 4 hours. I quite liked the end result. Will try it in eggs today!

Also, my result is more like farmer’s cheese than cottage cheese. The difference being the amount of moisture in the finished product.

The less moisture, the fewer carbs. Grok says 100g of this is 1-3g carbs.

Oh and, yeah. I like this better than cottage cheese.

When 75% cooked, season and turn down to low or you will probably start seeing burnt pieces.
About 15-20 minutes total.

recipes.title: Smoked Fall-Apart Meat
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
"All you eat is steak."

Anytime I want something I’m smoking to end up falling apart, this is the technique I use.

Smoke for two hours with indirect heat and then wrap in butcher paper and then foil and bake @ 250° until the internal temperature is 204° plus. 

You can use this technique totally in your oven. Just bake your meat on a grated rack at 250° for a few hours.

recipes.description:
Had some jalapeños I needed to get rid of, so I stuffed them with crab meat and they turned out better than I expected. 

If you don’t like jalapeños you can stuff shrooms. 

One cup lump crab
4 tbs Boursin cheese
2 tbs sour cream
1 tbs Old Bay

Topping:

1/2 cup coarse pork panko
2-4 tbs butter
1 tbs parm cheese

Bake or air fry at 375 for 15-20 minutes

recipes.title: Smoked Ribeyes
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
How I smoke my ribeyes:

Dry brine a 1” steak overnight. Use half a chimney of charcoal. Place wood on grate over hot coals. Place steak a few inches from the heat. Rotate after 12 minutes, flip after 24 minutes. Cook 12 more minutes and the sear over the coals.

Place lid over grill and close vents so you can save any unburnt wood. 

The closer you have the steak to the hot charcoal, the more done your steak will be. Back away a few inches if you want rare or medium rare.

recipes.title: Roasted Garlic
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Roasting garlic is so easy. This was made in the air fryer at 370° for about 50 minutes. You can do this in an oven, but it might take a little longer.

Decapitate the cloves to expose the top part of the garlic, lightly oil with avocado oil, or olive oil, lightly salt, and cover.

These little Le Creuset pots worked perfectly, but you can use any bakeware and cover with an aluminum tent if you don’t have one of these.

If you overcook the garlic a little bit, you get a wonderful caramelized type candy. This batch was 90% soft and 10% caramelized and truly a treat..

recipes.title: Pumpkin Cheesecake Dessert
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Low carb pumpkin dessert with a cheesecake whipped cream, if you are looking for a Thanksgiving dessert that won't beat you up too much.

It's somewhere between cake and pie and is about 30g of carbs if you use Allulose or Stevia as the sweetener.

1 cup pumpkin puree
1 cup butter powder
1 egg
1 tbs vanilla
Sweetener to taste

Use an immersion blender to get the butter powder fully incorporated. Place batter in a buttered ramekin or like sized pan. Bake at 375 for 40-50 minutes or until a toothpick comes back clean.

Topping: 
1/3 cup heavy cream
2 tbs mascarpone or cream cheese
1/2 tbs vanilla
sweetener of choice

Turned out really good!

recipes.title: Butter Powder Fathead Pizza
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Butter Powder Fathead Pizza turned out as good as I could have hoped.

Adding butter powder and gelatin doubled the sturdiness and using Boursin gave it a nice herby, garlicky flavor. 

Maybe a calzone in my future!

1.5 cups mozzarella 
2 tbs Boursin cheese

Microwave or double boiler cheeses in 30 second bursts until they combine smoothly.

Add 1 egg and then 1/2 to 1 cup butter powder (I was somewhere in the middle) and 1 tbs of beef or plain gelatin.

Bake at 400° for 12 minutes. Flip and bake another two minutes.

Don’t forget to grate extra cheese for your toppings!

recipes.title: Burnt Ends (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Here's a rough idea of how I made them. Will do a video on the burnt ends soon.

Cube a chuck roast into 2" pieces. Season and cook over indirect heat (approx 250 degrees) for 2 hours. Transfer to a pan, coat with butter, cover and bake about 1.25 hours. Drain most of the butter and coat with a sugar free BBQ (Primal Kitchens), return to oven for 10 minutes. Aiming for 205 internal temp.

Debone a short rib slab, season and cook over indirect heat for about 2 hours. Wrap in butcher paper and foil and cook at 250 in oven until 205 degrees. Took about 80 minutes.

recipes.title: Yorkshire Pudding
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I don't even know what Yorkshire pudding is supposed to taste like but I made this carnivore version and it turned out uniquely amazing. Something about how the tallow browns the crust gives it a taste that is indescribably delicious.

Carnivore Yorkshire Pudding:
Batter:
Mix 2 eggs
1/2 cup butter powder
1/2 cup heavy cream

Leave in fridge overnight

Bake muffin pan with a tsp of tallow in 7 bays at 425° for about 12 minutes or until wisps of smoke start to appear.

Fill each muffin bay halfway and bake 14-16 minutes. Try not to peak since this may deflate your pudding.

Each pudding is about .5 g carbs.

Drizzled with maple syrup may be dangerous so do so only if you have mastered your hormones!

recipes.title: Scotch Eggs (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I've tried to make my version of Scotch eggs before but found it too difficult to wrap the eggs with ground beef (instead of sausage). I learned it's much easier to wrap if I mix an egg in the ground beef.

These were delicious when cooked on the Weber for an hour with indirect heat and eaten with a homemade honey mustard.

Next time, I will use a fattier ground beef (this was 85%) to make them juicier and will try to start with boiled eggs that are less cooked. These eggs were 3 minute Instant Pot low pressure cooked and had jammy centers when I put these together.

Scotch eggs:
1.5 pounds ground beef
12 slices bacon
Favorite seasonings, salt
1 egg

Divide mixed ground beef or sausage into 6 even balls. Flatten and bury each soft boiled egg. Wrap each with 2 pieces of bacon.

Cook with indirect heat for about 15 minutes on each side.

Honey Mustard:
3 tbs sour cream
2 tbs mustard
1 tbs maple syrup or favorite sweetener
ingredients_raw: 1 tbs maple syrup or favorite sweetener

1 egg 
4 tbs butter powder  
1.5 tbs unsweetened cocoa  
1 tsp espresso powder  
1/2 tbs vanilla  
2 tbs melted butter 
Sweetener of choice  

Air fry 8 minutes at 350 or bake in oven at 350 for 15-20 minutes.  

To make an easy cream cheese whipped cream, use an immersion blender on 1/4 cup cream, sweetener, vanilla and 2 tbs cream cheese or mascarpone.

recipes.title: Crunchy-Top Dip
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
This tastes so good, especially with the crunchy top! I meant it to be a dip but it's good enough to eat with a fork, which I did.

Boursin Baked Crab Dip

I cup lump crab
2 tbs Boursin cheese
1 tbs sour cream
2 tbs butter
1 tbs parm cheese
1/2 cup pork panko (not fine)
A sprinkle of Old Bay

Combine seasoning, Boursin cheese and sour cream and place in one or two ramekins. If a one ramekin air fry this part for 5 minutes at 375 and then add the topping (melted butter, crumbs and parm cheese) and air fry to 8-10 minutes.

You can skip the 5-minute air frying stage if you use 2 ramekins. Just add the topping and air fry for about 10 minutes. I've done both and both turn out great.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Bacon Onion Ring Burgers
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Finally, an air fryer version of the bacon wrapped onion ring burgers! 

Freezing before wrapping makes it much easier to work with and keeps the ground beef juicy. 

The bacon is crisp. The ground beef is juicy and the onion is 80% cooked. https://t.co/hrxs7KR0iD
instructions: Divide 1 lb ground beef into 2 patties. Season the beef with salt and black pepper. Freeze the patties until they are firm so they hold their shape.
Cut 2 thick onion rings, wide enough for a patty to sit inside each ring.
Set one beef patty in each onion ring. Wrap each one with bacon, about 3 slices per patty (6 slices total).
Air fry at 375°F until the bacon is crisp, the beef is cooked through, and the onion is mostly soft, about 15 to 20 minutes. Turn once.
For the last 2 minutes, lay 1 slice of American cheese on each patty so it melts.
Serve with sugar-free ketchup, mustard, and dill pickle chips.

recipes.title: Gluten Free Biscuit Buns
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Here are some more gluten free “biscuit” options. As buns they do ok but as a vehicle for butter, they achieve the highest level of excellence.

Each of the three recipes is exactly the same, except the one using powdered milk gets a tablespoon of melted butter.

1 cup of powdered heavy cream, OR powdered goat milk OR powdered milk
1 egg
1 tsp baking powder

Bake at 350° on a parchment line sheet tray for 15 to 20 minutes. Each batch will yield two nice sized biscuits.

What’s interesting is that each variation gets a different texture. 

Powdered Heavy cream: slightly sweet, like Hawaiian rolls

Powdered Goat milk: a hint of sweetness and more like a biscuit

Powdered milk: crumbly like a scone on the outside, but textured like a biscuit on the inside.

Cook chicken in oven 15-20 minutes and then flip. Cook about 10 more minutes.

The marinara is simple. Just heat it enough to activate the garlic and herbs. Top with 1 cup mozzarella and put in the oven for 6-7 minutes.

Makes 2 servings.

recipes.title: General Cary's Beef (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I suppose this is Paleo Chinese.

As requested:

General Cary's Beef:
16-20 oz steak sliced thin
1/2 cup beef broth
2 tbs K Curious Pantry Gochujang
2 tbs rice vinegar
2 tbs No Soy Soy Free Sauce (Made by Halo)
or 2 tbs Coconut aminos
1 tbs fresh chopped garlic
1/2 tbs fresh ginger
2 tbs honey
1/2 tbs crushed red pepper
Zest from half an orange

Marinate overnight or up to 24 hours. Stir at least once to get all the pieces equal time in the sauce.

Cook at 12-15 under an oven broiler on a grated sheet pan or on the BBQ grill. Save any extra marinade to reapply to the finished product! Just add 3-4 tbs of honey to help thicken the sauce.

recipes.title: Ketchup
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Nice knowing you Heinz, but I found a simple way to make a clean ketchup that is lower in carbs and tastes great.

3 oz tomato paste  (1/2 small can)
1/4 cup apple cider vinegar 
2 tbs bone broth or water 
1/4 tsp garlic power 
1/4 tsp onion powder
1/4 tsp Stevia (or maple syrup)
salt to taste

Directions: Blend all ingredients with an immersion blender.

Yield: about 7 oz
Carb count: 2g per tablespoon

Notes: This version is fairly tangy. You can add less ACV and add more water or broth to control that. Customize the level of sweetness with your Stevia. Add less and taste it. You can always add more. AI says it should keep for 3 weeks. 

I only made a half can batch because I only use ketchup for 2 recipes (Big Mac Sauce and Sloppy Joes) and I just needed a small amount. Double this recipe for a full can.

recipes.title: Homemade Seasoning
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I get asked about what seasonings I use. For the past 4 months I've been making my own. It's not cheap because I pay for top quality spices but I love the results and a batch of this stuff lasts me for ages.

Half a bottle is about 1/4 cup so I do
1/4 c garlic powder
1/4 c onion powder
1/4 c paprika
1/4 c chili powder
1 tsp cayenne (optional)

I'll use this on everything but steaks for which I just prefer salt. 

It goes well on beef, pork and chicken. If I want to make taco bowls, I'll season the beef generously with this mix and add about a tbs of cumin per pound. 

I don't add salt to this because it doesn't pour as well as I want and I'm not adding sand like most spice companies do.

I like storing the spice in these parmesan dredge shakers which you can get in grocery stores and in most places that sell cheese.

recipes.title: Powdered Heavy Cream
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
So here’s my take on Anthony’s powdered heavy cream.

It works for my reduction gravy recipe and as a HC replacement in my dessert recipes but it does not fluff quite as much. The more powder you add, the thicker the fluff.

The taste is not quite as good as regular HC but it’s good enough as an ingredient and it doesn't have carrageenan. 

I had to double the amount of powder that the bag instructions said so it’s one cup of water to one cup powder. Lesser amounts don’t work as well. And I did let this "marinate" overnight before using as instructed by the directions.

You can also add this powder directly to whole milk for a similar result.

recipes.title: Crab Hush Puppies
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Carnivore Crab Hush Puppies:

The mix:
Half can (8 oz) crab (drained)
1/4 cup of melted butter
2-3 tbs Old Bay (optional)
Salt to taste

The breading:
1 cup pork panko
2 eggs

Lard or tallow to deep fry

Combine mix ingredients and form small balls. 
Freeze at least 1 hour.
Bread the balls and freeze again for 1 hour.
Bread the balls again for a second coating freeze for 1 hour.
Let the balls thaw in the fridge overnight.
Deep fry at 350° for 1.5-2 minutes.

Yield: 9 pups 

Notes: I may add even more butter to the mix next time. They weren't as buttery as I had hoped they would be. 

Add more Old Bay if you like. 

Freezing after the second coating may not be necessary.

I did some with a single coating and some with a double and the doubles were way better.

recipes.title: Deviled Eggs (3)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
This is the only way I will make deviled eggs from now on. It's easy, delicious and carnivore except for 1tbs of vinegar.

Ingredients: 
6 boiled eggs
1/4 cup bone broth (any kind)
1 tbs white vinegar
1.5 tbs cold butter
dash of salt

You can add 1/2-1 tbs yellow mustard if you want them tangier.

Halve the eggs and put the yolks in a container you can use an immersion blender with (I have a 2 cup Pyrex measuring cup). Add the remaining ingredients plus the whites from 2 eggs and mix well. Save the remaining 8 egg white halves to fill.

2.6g carbs per recipe

recipes.title: Cod Chowder
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Cod Chowder

1.5 pounds cod filet
2-6 oz cans dice clams with juice
16 oz clam juice
1 cup chopped onion
1 tbs garlic powder
1/2 tbs thyme
1/2 cup chopped peppers
1/2-pound chopped bacon
2 cups heavy cream
1/2 cup water
2 tbs butter

Chop and fry the bacon. Reserve the bacon for topping later. Cook the chopped onion and peppers about halfway in the bacon grease. 

Put all clam juice (save the clams for later) in a stock pot with garlic, thyme and salt. Add the cooked onions and peppers to the broth as well as the heavy cream and reduce on high for 15 minutes.

Add the clams and cod (cut into chunky pieces) and cook an additional 15 minutes. Add the butter near the end. 

Yields 6 generous portions at about 8gcarbs per serving.

recipes.title: Carnivore Crumbles (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
The crumbles:
4 oz melted butter
1/2 cup dry non fat milk

Melt butter on lowest heat possible. Sprinkle dry milk. Stir every 10 seconds or so until evenly caramelized. Took about 20 minutes of a gas stove.

The cheesecake batter:
8 oz soft cream cheese
8 oz soft mascarpone 
1.5 tbs vanilla 
2 tbs allulose 
3 room temp eggs

Mix the eggs last, one at a time. Pour into ramekins or baking dish lined with crumbles. I used two 5x7s but an 8x8 should work perfectly. Bake at 325 for 30-35 minutes or until set. Cool at room temp for 2 hours. Refrigerate at least 4 hours before cutting.

Icing: 1/2 cup heavy cream
2 tbs mascarpone 
1 tbs vanilla 
1 tbs allulose 

Whip about minutes or until stiff.

Cut cabbage into strips. Place in insta pot with 1 cup chicken broth (no trivet.) Add onions, your favorite seasoning, salt and 4 oz butter.

Cook on high pressure for 4 minutes with instant release.

1 Tbs salt

recipes.title: Bacon Cheeseburger Chili (1)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
So simple to make.

Bacon Cheeseburger Chili:
2 pounds ground beef
1 pound ground bacon
2 cups diced onion
6 cups beef stock
18 oz diced tomatoes
12 oz tomato paste
4 Tbs chili powder
3 Tbs cumin
2 Tbs garlic powder
2 Tbs paprika
1 Tbs cayenne 
1 Tbs black pepper
Salt to taste

Half cook onions in butter. Add grinds, drain grease. Combine all remaining ingredients and simmer for about 90 minutes.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese Flatbread
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
This cottage cheese flatbread recipe is all over YouTube so I had to give it a try. 

It’s 1 cup cottage cheese mixed in the food processor with 2 eggs. I added a half cup of mozzarella cheese to try and make it stronger.

Verdict: as a pizza crust, I wasn’t impressed. It’s still pretty flimsy and didn’t make a good hot pizza but it did taste decent as cold pizza, because crust isn’t important when you’re eating cold pizza. You can’t taste the cottage cheese. 

I might try this again as a wrap.

recipes.title: Salmon (1)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
What's your favorite salmon? This wild caught Copper River Sockeye was the best I ever had. It's a little pricey @ $25/lb but it stole the spotlight at dinner!

Why so expensive? It's highly coveted and is only harvested for a few months of the year. I used a Northwoods Fire seasoning and butter to blacken it. Highly recommend this fish!!

Pro tip: Aim for 140° internal for perfectly cooked salmon.

recipes.title: Goat
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
First time eating goat. I had these in the instant pot for 30 minutes after seasoning with a Northwoods fire seasoning. Finished with butter in a hot skillet.

I wasn’t crazy about the result, but I could definitely survive on it if I had to. It tastes like 50% lamb 30% beef and 20% pork. It’s not quite a strong tasting as lamb and the fat draws in a lot of good flavor with the seasonings!

The sauce is a black garlic butter mayo which hooked it up nicely.

To be fair, these were frozen chunks and who knows how much better it would’ve been from the choice parts of the goat?

Eating Instant Pot pork belly feels like my taste buds rode an exciting new ride in the amusement park. It's incomparable!

It has the texture of a perfectly cooked chuck roast, a light porky flavor that reminds of the most bacony ribs you've ever tasted and the fat melts in your mouth with just the slightest encouragement by tongue and teeth.

You must try this!

recipes.title: Soup du Jour
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I used to make a soup du jour for a privately owned Italian restaurant and one of the most popular was stuffed cabbage soup. I made it for the first time in a decade today but I replaced the rice with cauliflower.

6 cups beef broth
1.5 lbs ground beef, drained
18 oz crushed tomatoes 
Half head cabbage
1 diced medium onion
2 cups cauliflower 
1 T garlic powder
2 T fresh thyme
Salt to taste

Combine all ingredients and cook until veg are soft.

recipes.description:

recipes.description:

-sprinkle powdered collagen as a binder 
-dip in egg
-coat lightly in pork rind crumbs
-freeze for at least 2 hours
-bake on grated rack @ 400° for about 12 minutes

The crust is not quite as crispy as I would like. Need to fry a few in lard or tallow next time.

3 quarts seafood stock
1 medium red snapper 
4 tablespoons Biden pepper flakes
1 tablespoon cayenne
1/2 pound scallops

Add all and cook on medium for about 30 minutes. Add scallops and only cook those about 12 minutes.

recipes.title: Poached Eggs (2)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Poached eggs in the shell via sous vide.

1) lower refrigerated eggs gently into 167°F sous vide bath and cook for 14 minutes exactly.

2) remove and cool in iced water for least 5 minutes.

3) use the back of a butter knife and crack around the center of the egg. Gently dump it out.

Notes: you will see a few jiggly whites, but that’s just parts that have fallen off and they are fully cooked. Part of the whites may stick to the inside of the eggshell but it just means more yolk, which is a positive thing for me. #worldcarnivoremonth #carnivorediet #EggWeek

recipes.title: Egg Salad (3)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Egg salad with just eggs and salt!

1) Soft boil eggs for seven minutes 15 seconds. That’s straight from fridge to boiling water.

2) Cool eggs for five minutes in ice water and then peel.

3) Place eggs in a bowl and mash with a fork or the tip of a whisk. Add salt to taste.
 
Notes: Serve with bacon for best results!

#WorldCarnivoreMonth #carnivorediet #EggWeek

[self-reply] First off, don't make this! 😂 It's good but a pain in the ass. I soaked it overnight in a cup of buttermilk mixed with 1 egg, after cutting it up into tubes. Drained it, sprinkled with powdered collagen and then back into marinade and then into seasoned pork panko. The heat is crucial and needs to be around medium and here's the worst part: it likes to explode like popcorn and splatters grease geysers as high as 3-4 feet about the pan. Sometimes the calamari even jumps out of the pan. 

The sauce is Yellow Bird jalapeno sauce.

recipes.title: Dry Brined Burgers
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Now I know I told ya'll not to dry brine ground beef (mince) because numerous internet sources said not to. So I did anyway because I'm stubborn. Results after 24 hours:

Control burger was smaller with a less defined sear. The salt from the DB burger came from inside the burger as opposed to seeming like a topping. The flavors were comparable and the DB burger may have been a tiny bit less chewy. The DB burger also cooked faster despite being bigger.

All in all , DB didn't hurt the burger and I'm curious to hear what others might think. #carnivorediet #Yes2meat

This batch yielded 5 pieces of 1/2"x2" chocolate at a total cost of $6 with each piece having just under 10g carbs. Recipe, ingredients links and a photo of my setup in the following posts. #chocolatier

1/4

recipes.title: Fried Fish & Pseudo Grits
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Fried fish and pseudo grits with bacon for brunch today. The flounder was dredged w/gelatin, dipped in egg and then pork panko-en before getting baked at 350° for about 30 minutes and turned out great! 

The “grits” are cooked egg whites, sour cream, gelatin, butter, salt and garlic powder. It was a failed attempt to make carnivore mashed potatoes but ended up closer to grits! They were definitely better than cauliflower mash! 

Sometimes a failure is a different kind of success! I look forward to trying the grits with scrambled eggs and bacon and will put up a recipe when I finally get it the way I want it.

recipes.title: $10 Meal

recipes.description:

recipes.title: Oven Bacon
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description: I get asked a lot about how I cook my bacon and I prefer to cook it in the oven in a foil and parchment paper lined roasting pan (Pyrex works) for consistency and easy cleanup. I cook mine at 375° F for about 30 minutes. After the grease has cooled a little, I pick up the foil and pour the grease into a storage container for future use. The roasting pan needs no cleaning if I do it right!

recipes.title: White Pizzagna
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I made White Pizzagna tonight to test two theories:

1) Does it taste good without tomatoes (which would make it carnivore)?
2) Can I put the tomatoes on after it's done baking so I don't have to deal with the water that leeches out of them?

The answers are not that great and yes! The tomatoes really brings all the ingredients together. Another alternative I may try is straining the chopped tomatoes for 15 minutes before adding them. 

For now Pizzagna stays #keto for me. Feel free to try it and let me know what you think. #RealFood #Yes2meat Recipe next tweet

recipes.title: Smoked Chuck Roast (1)
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Best chuck roast of my life and there's still room for improvement. I smoked this at 180° for 3 hours, aiming for an internal of 160-165°, then wrapped it butcher paper and foil, increased temp to 250° and cooked it for 1 hour (internal 190°). I should have just stopped there but I cooked it another 30 minutes at 250° and I think all that did was leech some of the moisture. 

The flavor and texture were perfect though. It had the texture of the most tender steak and the hickory didn't overwhelm the beefy flavor. #CarnivoreDiet #Keto #LCHF #Yes2Meat #RealFood

recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:

~With an immersion blender, combine 3 egg yolks with 6T room temperature (soft) butter to get a more mayo like consistency. Roll the extra BM in parchment paper and refrigerate. Slice into coins as needed.

I use this on eggs, lean steaks and ham, mostly. There are unlimited ways on how you can use this Lazy Man's Hollandaise.

recipes.title: Tender Roast
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
I'll be eating more roasts after I finally found a method that leaves it tender but not mushy. This 2.26lb 7 bone chuck was dry brined for 3 days (2 would have been fine) and smoked at 180°F for 2.5 hours, wrapped in butcher paper and foil and cooked in its own juices for another 2 hours @ 225°F.

To repeat this in an oven: 
Slow cook uncovered @ 200-225° until roast hits 150-160°
Then wrap and cook until it hits 210°
Total cook time is about 2 hours per pound.
#carnivore #carnivorediet #yes2meat #keto #RealFood

recipes.title: Dry Brined Pork Ribs
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
There is no sauce on these ribs! 

I was only able to put a 12 hour dry brine on this 6.8 lb rack of pork ribs but after I modified the 3/2/1 method in my smoker, these ribs turned out amazing. The skinny side bark was a tiny bit chewy but not in an unpleasant way, the fat along the left side was crunchy and the meat on the thick side was succulent. It was a banquet of textures.

I went 3/1/1 and if you don't know what that means, it's 3 hours uncovered in the smoker at 225°, 1 hour wrapped in butcher paper, then foil and then 1 hour uncovered + 30 minutes at 400° for more color. And from what I understand, this method works in the oven too.

Did I say there is no sauce on these ribs?  See video in next tweet to show you how tender they were and why I went 3/1/1.
#Carnivore #carnivorediet #keto #lchf #Yes2Meat #RealFood

recipes.title: Steak Pan Sear
recipes.author: CaryKelly11
recipes.description:
Life's too short to eat a steak w/ a bad pan sear. Here's how to avoid that: (THREAD)

1) You need a good frying pan. Cast iron is the best bcz of how well it distributes heat. Stainless works decently. Pans w/ non-stick surfaces work ok but have debatable safety ratings.

1/6 https://t.co/pFH7WutktQ

instructions.text: You need a good frying pan. Cast iron is the best bcz of how well it distributes heat. Stainless works decently. Pans w/ non-stick surfaces work ok but have debatable safety ratings.
Dry your steak and then season it with your favorite spices. I typically use just garlic powder and salt. Sometimes a seasoned salt and sometimes Canadian.

You need the right amount of heat on your pan. 80% of max is perfect on my stove. Add 1/4 cup of oil to your pan as it heats. (I like avocado oil due to high smoke point. Other oils work too). Add 2 tbs butter. When butter's melted and starting to brown, add steak.

Ensure the contact point is well greased by moving the steak around and wait... for about 4 minutes. Peel the steak back but not completely away from the pan to see if the sear is to your desired specs. Flip it or drop it back down, accordingly.

Store-bought taco seasoning is trash. Here's a guilt-free version you can make at home.

4 Tbs chili powder
3 Tbs paprika
3 Tbs cumin
1 Tbs salt
1 Tsp onion powder
1 Tsp garlic power
1 Tsp black pepper
1/8 tsp cayenne

Use 3 Tbs per lb or ground beef. More or less if you like.

recipes.title: How to Dry Brine
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Pat meat dry.
Salt both sides a little more than usual
Refrigerate uncovered for 24 hours for steak.
Use more salt and go 48 hours for thicker cuts of meat, like roasts
If you see salt on your meat after 12 hours, brush off the excess.
If it’s damp, add a little more.

recipes.title: How to smoke a steak:
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Smoke at 250F degrees for 20-25 minutes per pound of meat or until internal temp reaches 128-130 degrees for medium rare.
Reverse sear in a skillet with your favorite butter/oil (I use butter and tiny bit of avocado oil to raise the smoke point) for about 30 seconds on each side.
Small steaks will be harder, but not impossible, to keep from being medium well or well done.
Thicker cuts are optimal!

instructions.text: Cold or hot smoke your favorite kosher or fine salt in ANY type of grill. 3 hours will give some flavor, 8 will give you color and amazing flavor. The torch is for lighting the pellets in your smoke tube.

recipes.title: Smoked Oxtail
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Slightly caramelized on the outside, tender on the inside and barely hanging onto the bone, this oxtail recipe begins with a 48-72 hour dry brine.
Smoke at 180°F until internal reaches 165°. This took 4 hours for me.
Put oxtails in metal or Pyrex pan and cover with parchment paper then foil and cook at 225° for another 4-5 hours or until internal temperature reaches 202°
There’s no reason this method won’t work in the oven. This method works for ribs and roasts also. The key is to aim for these temperatures. Cooking times will vary.

recipes.title: Maryland Style Shrimp
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Miss spicy food on low carb?
Maryland style shrimp might be your ticket.
There are a lot more complex recipes on the Internet but adding 2 tablespoons of Old Bay for every pound of shrimp cocktail does the trick for me.
Not hot enough?
Add some Cayenne Pepper.
You can buy pre-cooked shrimp or if you want to save a few dollars, you can buy it raw and deveined.
Simply peel and boil your shrimp 3-4 minutes from frozen and cool down immediately in cold water or an ice bath.
Then peel your shrimp and add the spices.

recipes.title: Smoked or Baked Chuck Roast
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: I cook this the same way I cook my brisket but a Chuck roast takes a lot less time.
Start with a 2-day dry brine and then smoke or bake at 180°F for about 3 hours or until internal temp reaches 152-155°.
Then wrap roast in butcher or parchment paper and wrap again in foil to create a braising chamber.
Turn up heat to 250° and cook until it reaches 202°.
This should take 1.5-2 hours depending on how big the roast is.
Cooking it beyond this point will dry it out.
Allow 15-20 minutes for roast to rest before slicing.

recipes.title: Carnivore Burger Bun
recipes.author: ckelly1969
recipes.description: This glorified chaffle bun is the best no flour bun I’ve ever eaten. It’s sturdy, has eye appeal and doesn’t taste eggy.
ingredients_raw: 2 oz soft goat cheese or cream cheese

ingredients.raw: 2 oz soft goat cheese or cream cheese
ingredients.item: soft goat cheese or cream cheese

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375° F. Combine all ingredients except butter, in small mixing bowl with a whisk or fork. Melt 1/2 T butter in 4-4″ baking pans in oven and make sure the butter thoroughly coats the bottom and sides of each baking pan. Split your batter between the 4 pans and return to the oven for about 12 minutes. Flip the buns over and bake another 5 minutes. The “buns” should fall right out of the pans.

notes: You can make this with just mozzarella and eggs but it tastes pretty eggy. You can use two 4×9″ bread pans to make one large pair of rectangular buns… perhaps ideal for a Philly cheesesteak! You can just cook this batter in your waffle iron if you like but I wanted something that would hold a big boy burger and the 4″ pans worked perfect to hold 1/2 lb burgers.

*Update: For a stiffer bun, an even better taste and 1 less gram of carbs, omit the goat cheese/cream cheese and add 2 tbs mascarpone cheese, 1 tbs unflavored gelatin and use an immersion blender to mix thoroughly

recipes.title: 97% Dark Chocolate
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Set up a double boiler (You can use a pot filled with boiling water and a small silicon or stainless bowl atop the pan), grate 1-2 cups of cocoa butter and add to pan, melting thoroughly, add cacao (or cocoa) powder and melt thoroughly. The mixture should be smooth and able to be poured slowly. Add 1 T Stevia or your favorite sweetener and 1 T vanilla and stir frequently until the Stevia is fully dissolved. If your mixture is too thick, add more cocoa butter. Pour into a candy mold and allow 2-4 hours to fully set. Should keep for about a week at room temp or in the fridge and in the freezer indefinitely.

notes: The recipes I researched called for 1 cup to 1 cup of cocoa butter to cacao powder but this ended up way too thick so I kept adding cocoa butter until the mixture was right.

recipes.title: No Flour Carnivore Gravy
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Reduce 2 cups of stock and 1 cup of heavy cream at 60% heat for about 30 minutes, stirring frequently.

notes: Use broth or stock. Drippings work too but too much grease will make a thin and streaky gravy.
You can reduce at lower heat but cook time will take much longer. Just be wary that untended pans may overflow at higher heats because of the cream.
Add garlic and onion powder if you like.

You may or may not want to add salt. I find the salt in the stock to be enough to flavor this. If you do add salt, do it AFTER it’s finished reducing. The salt in the stock will intensify as it reduces.

recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°. Saute celery and onion in melted butter until soft. Grind pork rinds in food processor until pieces are pebble sized and smaller. Do not use the darker or harder pieces. Harder pieces will end up chewy. Combine all ingredients and mix thoroughly. Pack loosely and bake in a Pyrex or baking pan for 20-25 minutes. The pan pictured here is 7.25″ x 5.5″.

notes: Makes 2 servings. A 3.25 oz bag of pork rinds = 2 cups of pork rind crumbs. The amount of stock you need varies according to how finely you grind the pork rind crumbs. The mixture should be wet enough to form crumbly cakes if you were to pack them. Use the best tasting, unflavored pork rinds you can find. The fresh rosemary and thyme really complete the dish. Dried herbs will work though. Goes great with my gravy reduction recipe available on this site.

recipes.title: Dr. Roth’s Keto Cappuccino Chocolate Chunk Ice Cream Brownie (20g carbs per serving)
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Heat cream, cocoa powder and vanilla extract in a sauce pan until it comes to a slight boil. Remove from heat and let cool for about 2minutes. Pour into a mixer cup, add egg yolks and lukewarm coffee and combine thoroughly with an immersion blender. Pour liquid in a shallow pie pan and stir in and melt 1/3 cup (Half the total amount of) chocolate chips (I used a 6″ pie pan) and place in freezer for 45 minutes. Mix in the other 1/3 cup of chocolate chips after product has cooled for 45 minutes so the chips don’t melt. Return to the freezer for at least 2 hours.

notes: if you want just ice cream, you can skip melting in the first 1/3 cup of chips. The finished product is rock hard with the full recipe. I heated the bottom of the pan for about 60 seconds on a stove burner and gently used a butter knife to separate the product from the edges, then flipped the pan onto a cutting board to free it from the pan. It was then easy to cut into wedges. You can microwave the end result for 20 seconds to give it a warm brownie texture but I enjoyed it best while fully frozen. Makes 2 servings

Directions: Pan sear all chicken in hot animal fat and add to a stock pot with 1/2 gallon chicken stock or water, add all other ingredients and boil at medium heat for about 1.5 hours or until the chicken is tender and falls off the bone.
Notes: Any part of the chicken will work. I used a half chicken, bones and all. The result will end up almost stew like so add more liquid if you want it soupier. Gochugaru is the powdered pepper used to make kimchi. It makes my mouth warm but not hot because there are no sharp edges to the heat. You may want to start with 2 Ts of Gochugaru before deciding on a 3rd.

recipes.title: Chuck Roast Soup (1)
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: After a 2-day dry brine, cut roast into big chunks and give them a quick sear in a skillet with animal fat.
Place roast pieces in Dutch oven, baking dish or slow cooker and add beef broth or water.

In the pan drippings, cook rough chopped onions about halfway along with smashed garlic cloves but add the garlic at the very end so you don’t burn it. Add garlic and onions to the pot and slow cook, covered, on low for 4 hours or until the roast chunks are almost fork tender.

Rough chop the cabbage and thick slice the zucchini and mushrooms. This will all get added at the 4 hour mark. Allow to cook another 1 – 1.5 hours or until the vegetables are just soft. Salt to taste.

notes: When serving, shred the beef with 2 forks for best results.

recipes.title: Butter Chicken (2)
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Ingredients
Cut chicken into large bite sized pieces and coat with all seasonings. Mix thoroughly and refrigerate covered, overnight.

Cook chicken in skillet with a little animal fat. Make sure to scrape the bottom to get all the essence into play. While you’re doing that, dice and cook your half onion in a tablespoon of butter until soft.

Add 2 Tablespoons of butter to the fully cooked chicken and the cooked onions. Add 1/2 cup cream (more or less according to preference) and keep stirring on medium heat until everything comes together. Should take 1-2 minutes.

notes: Omit the cayenne or add more if you want this dish spicier. Typical butter chicken has the spice Garam Masala but I couldn’t find any on short notice so I omitted it. It still tasted great without it.
Too much butter makes the sauce more likely to break. Best eaten fresh. Reheating will break the sauce which you could maybe avoid if you add more cream when you reheat it in a skillet.

recipes.title: Carnivore White Pizzagna
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Cook ground beef and add seasonings to taste. Mix ricotta cheese with 1 egg and seasonings to taste. Combine and heat 1 cup heavy cream, 4 tbs Boursin cheese and 4 tbs parm cheese. Heat until smooth like gravy.

Layer ground beef, ricotta mix, Boursin Alfredo, mozzarella cheese and then pepperoni, in a small cast iron skillet or pie pan. Heat under broiler for a few minutes or until the cheese and pepperoni are to your liking.

Directions: Cook ground beef and add seasonings to taste. Mix ricotta cheese with 1 egg and seasonings to taste. Combine and heat 1 cup heavy cream, 4 tbs Boursin cheese and 4 tbs parm cheese. Heat until smooth like gravy.

recipes.title: Korean Honey BBQ Wings (2)
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: Coat chicken with a little avocado oil and season with garlic powder and onion powder.
Cook on parchment lined sheet tray at 400 for 40-45 minutes.
Coat wings in BBQ sauce and return to oven for 10 more minutes. 66g carbs.
This is enough sauce for 40 medium wings. 10/10!

recipes.title: Brisket style short ribs
recipes.author: ckelly1969

instructions.text: A 4-5 pound short rib section. Your favorite rub and salt. I used garlic powder, onion powder and salt.

Remove the bones and season thoroughly. Slow cook on a grated rack at 250° for about 5 hours. Wrap in butcher paper and cook another 2 hours at 300° or until internal temp reaches 202+. Let rest 30 minutes without unwrapping.

recipes.label: CUSTOM RECIPE
recipes.title: Shrimp Boursin
adapted_from: Diabetic Chef Keto Creamed Firecracker Shrimp (https://diabeticchefsrecipes.com/keto-creamed-firecracker-shrimp/)
recipes.description: Custom recipe: shrimp in a garlic-herb Boursin cream sauce with lemon and a chipotle 'firecracker' kick. Boursin sauce base from KetoCarnivore9, shrimp method, lemon and chipotle from Diabetic Chef's Creamed Firecracker Shrimp.

ingredients.raw: 1/4 t chipotle powder (starting point; add more to taste)
2 C cooked spaghetti squash or sauteed zucchini (optional, to serve)

instructions: Heat butter until bubbling and just starting to brown.
Quickly saute shrimp until just pink; set aside.
In the same pan, add heavy cream and Boursin; stir over medium heat until melted and smooth.
Stir in lemon juice and chipotle powder; taste and adjust.
Simmer until it reaches the thickness you like.
Return shrimp to the pan and toss to coat.
Serve over spaghetti squash or zucchini; top with chives.
